meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here about the zero on Owen's essay, and who decided it.
I don't have time for this. The zero stands.
You asked for this meeting, Hale. "The zero stands" isn't a reason. On what basis, and was Owen heard before it went in?
Sorry. That came out wrong. Let me show you what I actually have: the essay quotes a line that isn't in Hamlet, and his October 15 outline argued cowardice, which the essay never mentions.
Students change their argument between an outline and a final draft; that's called writing. The line you say isn't in Hamlet, show me, on the page, with the play open next to it.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero on Owen's essay withdrawn, an apology, and the line you say is not in Hamlet shown to me on the page, beside the play. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, having agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and the misquoted line shown to her against the play; that is not the fair outcome, which would be a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and the meeting ended before her time ran out.
What moved her: nothing; you named two specific pieces of evidence after your apology, but she had not been able to check either one yet.
What cost ground: you opened by saying you had no time and the zero stood, which refused her the reason and made her sharper before you had shown anything.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence never came near a late night, since the only date you gave was the October 15 outline; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she asked to see the line on the page, put the essay's quotation next to the play right then, so she had something dated and tied to Owen's work that she could check herself.
